title: Customer evidence roadmap - technical appendix
body:
Purpose and audience:

This appendix is intended as the technical companion to the customer-facing evidence packet. Primary readers: customer security engineers and our Solutions Engineering (SE) leads who are preparing questionnaire responses and evidence bundles. It focuses on the items customers ask for most often: RBAC design and proof, audit-log schema and retention, SIEM ingestion samples, and the evidence automation plan for recurring questionnaire requests.

High-level summary (one paragraph):
Redwood Inference implements a role-based access control model (RBAC v2) that separates policy (roles, permissions), directory bindings (groups/SCIM), and runtime enforcement at the service gateway and data plane. Audit telemetry is emitted in a structured, searchable JSON schema; export adapters are available for common SIEMs (Splunk, Sumo Logic, Datadog, Azure Sentinel). Evidence automation pipelines produce evidence artifacts (policy snapshots, role-assignment CSVs, aggregated audit samples) on-demand for customer assessments.

Sections below are intentionally concise; SEs can copy/paste into customer responses and attach the referenced artifacts.

1) RBAC v2 - engineer-facing summary:
- Goals: minimal-privilege defaults, deterministic permission evaluation, scoping for org/customer/route, and auditability of grants.
- Core concepts:
  - Role: named collection of permissions (e.g., viewer, app-executor, admin).
  - Permission: fine-grained action (e.g., model.invoke, logs.read, billing.view).
  - Binding: mapping between principals (users/service-accounts/groups) and roles with an optional scope (org, project, model).
  - Scope: hierarchical, supports org -> project -> resource.
- Enforcement points: control-plane (management operations) and data-plane gateway (runtime token checks).
- Key proofs customers ask for: role definitions snapshot, binding exports, example evaluation trace for a sample request. We keep versioned snapshots in the evidence store.

RBAC v2 notes / gotchas (for internal SEs):
- We support temporary elevation (time-limited bindings) for on-call remediation flows. Provide example TTLed binding CSV from evidence pipeline when asked.
- SCIM sync: mapped attributes and group-remapping rules live in config repo (link above). If a customer wants SCIM mappings, include a sanitized export.

2) Audit log schema (short):
We emit structured audit events with a compact JSON schema. Below is the canonical field list and a small example. Fields are indexed for search and retained according to contract (default 90 days for hosted, configurable for Dedicated/Private).

Canonical fields: event_id, timestamp_utc, tenant_id, principal_id, principal_type, action, resource_type, resource_id, request_id, ip_address, user_agent, outcome, request_payload_hash, kv_cache_snapshot (optional), model_version, serving_node, region, latency_ms, trace_id

Example event (single-line representation customers can ingest):
{
  "event_id": "evt_8f9a1b",
  "timestamp_utc": "2025-01-09T14:22:33Z",
  "tenant_id": "org-123",
  "principal_id": "svc-account-45",
  "principal_type": "service_account",
  "action": "model.invoke",
  "resource_type": "model",
  "resource_id": "redwood/gptx-3.1",
  "request_id": "req_990e2",
  "ip_address": "18.205.33.14",
  "user_agent": "redwood-client-go/1.4.0",
  "outcome": "success",
  "request_payload_hash": "sha256:ab12...",
  "model_version": "2024-12-01",
  "serving_node": "gpu-pool-7",
  "region": "us-west-2",
  "latency_ms": "112",
  "trace_id": "trace-8aa2"
}

Retention and access model:
- Hosted: rolling default 90 days, customer can request exports.
- Dedicated/Private: retention and storage controlled by customer deployment, we provide export tooling and evidence packages.

3) SIEM export / mapping guidance:
- Formats supported: JSON over HTTPS, Syslog (CEF/LEEF via connector), S3 exports (bulk).
- Recommended ingestion pattern for real-time: push JSON events to customer-owned HTTPS endpoint or to a customer-managed ingestion buffer (SQS/Kinesis).
- Mapping sample (field -> Splunk):
  - event_id -> _raw/event_id
  - timestamp_utc -> _time (index as epoch)
  - tenant_id -> tenant_id (saved as tag)
  - principal_id -> user
  - action -> event_action
  - outcome -> result
  - resource_type/resource_id -> resource
  - trace_id/request_id -> correlation_id
- Attachments to include when responding:
  - siem-sample-events.json (100 anonymized events, spaced across 30 days)
  - siem-splunk-raw-index-example.txt (example ingestion record)
  - siem-connector-deployment-notes.md

4) Evidence automation plan (how we generate bundles):
- Trigger: on-demand via SE portal or automated weekly run for enterprise customers.
- Artifacts created: role-definitions-YYYYMMDD.csv, bindings-YYYYMMDD.csv, audit-sample-YYYYMMDD.json (configurable sample size), access-review-report-YYYYMMDD.pdf, schema.json (current audit schema).
- Sanitization: PII and customer-sensitive payloads are hashed/stripped. We include hashes for request bodies and can provide redacted copies under NDA.
- Storage and transit: artifacts are stored in an internal S3 bucket with limited access (ACL logs) and transport uses customer-specific secure links (pre-signed S3 or customer-only HTTPS).

5) Common questionnaire Q&A snippets (copy/paste):
Q: "Describe your access control model and how privileges are assigned"
A: "Redwood uses a role-based model (RBAC v2). Roles are collections of permissions that are bound to principals (users, groups, or service accounts) with optional scoping at org/project/model level. Bindings and role definitions are exported from our config repository and are recorded in versioned snapshots pulled into the evidence store. See attachment: role-definitions-2025-01-10.csv and binding-export-2025-01-10.csv."

Q: "How do you ensure audit logs are tamper-evident?"
A: "All audit events are signed with an internal HMAC and stored in append-only storage with write-ahead logs. Exported samples include integrity metadata and checksums for validation. For Dedicated/Private, we provide configuration guidance for external write-once stores on the customer side."

Q: "Can we receive SIEM-compatible stream of events?"
A: "Yes — we support JSON over HTTPS and S3 bulk export. We will provide a sample connector config and 100 anonymized events for ingestion testing. See attachment: siem-sample-events.json."

6) Attachments to prepare prior to customer handoff (SE checklist):
- role-definitions-YYYYMMDD.csv (sanitized)
- bindings-YYYYMMDD.csv (include TTL flags where used)
- audit-sample-YYYYMMDD.json (anonymized 100 events)
- siem-connector-deployment-notes.md
- evidence-manifest-YYYYMMDD.json (manifest listing artifacts and checksums)

7) Planned follow-ups / open items for engineering (short list):
- [ ] Implement 'export-preview' endpoint to allow SE to preview sanitized binding exports without manual ops intervention. Ticket: SEC-5028.
- [ ] Add HMAC fingerprint to exported manifest (engineering PR open: platform#342).
- [ ] Create a Splunk ingestion playbook with example props/transforms (owner: Marco).
- [ ] Confirm retention configuration and documentation for Dedicated customers (owner: Emily).

Notes to SEs (copy guidance):
- When sending evidence to customers, always include the evidence-manifest and the export checksum file. If the customer requests deeper fidelity (e.g., full request payloads), escalate to Legal & Security and proceed only under NDA.
- For questionnaire responses, use the Q&A snippets above and attach the corresponding artifact names.

Revision history / authorship:
- Drafted by Priya Das (product-security) 2025-01-10
- Added SIEM mapping and examples by Marco Ruiz 2025-01-22
- Reviewed by Emily Zhang (privacy) 2025-02-12

Slack/PR references (for SEs):
- Slack thread: #sec-evidence (link to anchor in Slack)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/342 (manifest HMAC)
- Jira: SEC-4921 (RBAC v2 rollout), SEC-5028 (export-preview)

Appendix A - quick audit-schema diffs to prior version (for engineers):
- Added fields: serving_node, model_version, request_payload_hash, kv_cache_snapshot (optional)
- Renamed: actor_id -> principal_id (to clarify multiple principal types)

End of appendix.

-- Priya Das (product-security)
